text: Study Sources 1 to 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘It is good to transport food over long distances.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘People now eat a wider range of food than they did in the past.’
How could you test this claim? You may consider the types of information, sources of evidence
or methods you might use.

text: Study Source 3.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one prediction from Adib’s statement. Explain why this is a prediction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why Hani’s statement might be biased.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Hani’s or Adib’s?
Your answer should consider both arguments and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different kinds of information used.

text: Study Source 4.
Your government wants to reduce pollution from transporting food over long distances.
The following suggestions have been made:
• offer more funding to local food producers
• launch an advertising campaign about pollution caused by food transportation
• increase taxes on food transported from other countries.
Which one of these would you recommend to the government, and why?
In your answer, you should:
• state your recommendation
• give reasons and evidence to support your choice
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
• consider different arguments and perspectives.
